title: fix(sim): the hole-wall excuse measures a facet about its hole's axis, so a tool cutting into a flat is a gouge
body:
## What changed

The containment kinds' hole-wall excuse in the solid law (drill, bore, thread mill, cross drill) read a facet by its **corners** against the **tool's own disc** (`swept.rs` `chord_dip`). If every vertex stood outside the tool, the facet was forgiven its edges' dip into it. That bound grows as the tool shrinks against the hole. Every flat whose corners lie on the hole circle (an octagon, a D-bore, a square) passes inside that circle along its middle, and a cut there got no blocking warning.

Now:
- The operation names its holes' axes: `verify::solid_hits_walled(path, facets, cutter, law, &[HoleAxis])`. `generate::contain_into` passes the op's Drill/Bore/Thread holes, and `cross_part` passes the cross holes' lines. `solid_hits` is unchanged for every other caller. With no holes named, nothing is excused.
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/hole_wall.rs`. A facet is excused only when it is a **round wall** of one of those holes. Its sagitta about the hole axis must be at most `WALL_SAG` = 0.05 mm. The sagitta is the nearest vertex's radius less the facet's **nearest approach** to the axis (point-to-segment, or point-in-triangle, in the plane square to the axis).
- The excuse granted is the smaller of that sagitta and the old edge-dip bound, so the law can only convict more than before, never less.
- A facet with any non-finite coordinate excuses nothing. So does a facet over the axis, or a hole axis that is not along the move's tool axis (`Frame::axis_xy`).
- `chord_dip` is removed. The decisions are in `docs/decisions/1205-hole-wall-nearest-point.md`: why a cap is needed on top of the nearest-point reading, why 0.05 mm, and what was dropped.

Why there is a cap: an octagon *is* an inscribed polygon of its corners' circle, with a 0.38 mm sagitta on r 5. So a nearest-point measurement alone still excuses a cut to its corners. Only a stated bound on what counts as tessellation tells a coarse circle from a flat. That is the issue's "passes inside the circle by more than the stated tolerance convicts".

## Probe readings (before = main's rule, after = this PR; the same build with the old rule toggled by a throwaway switch, since removed)

| Case (plate, blind hole, corners on the circle) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Thread mill 6 mm p1, declared r 4.4 (major 4.94), octagon on r 5: solid law | **0** gouges | 38 |
| same, D-bore (96-gon r 5, flat chord at Y 4) | **0** | 22 |
| same, 32-gon at the major circle (the thread's own round wall) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore EM-0600 at r 5, octagon on r 5 (0.38 mm into each flat): op verdict | **0** | 10 |
| Bore at r 5, D-bore | **0** | 4 |
| Bore at r 5, 32-gon on r 5 (0.024 mm sagitta, past the 0.01 tolerance) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore at r 4.6, octagon on r 5 (inside the 4.62 flats) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore at r 5, 23-gon (sagitta 0.0466, under the cap) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore at r 5, 22-gon (sagitta 0.0509, over the cap) | 0 | 10 |
| Drill DR-0600, octagon on r 3 (flats at 2.77) | **0** | 1 |
| Drill DR-0600, 32-gon on r 3 | 0 | 0 |

Thread note: on main, a model-sourced **Thread op** is already refused by its region law (the helix cuts past the declared minor circle by design; that is #1071, which PR #1099 grants). So the op-level probe gives 52 blocking warnings before and after. The reviewer's 0 was read on #1099's tree. The thread rows above therefore judge the generator's own helix with the solid law alone, as `contain_into` runs it. That is the verdict that stands once #1099 lifts the region law.

## Tests

- New `crates/app/tests/hole_wall_flats.rs` (4 tests):
  - `a_thread_mill_cutting_into_an_octagons_flats_is_a_gouge`: the reviewer's probe, plus the D-bore and the round-wall control.
  - `a_bore_or_drill_into_an_octagons_flats_is_a_gouge`
  - `a_round_tool_in_a_finely_faceted_round_hole_still_verifies_clean`
  - `the_wall_excuse_ends_at_its_stated_sagitta`: the boundary pin, 23-gon clean / 22-gon convicts on r 5.
- New unit tests in `hole_wall.rs`: `a_chord_reads_its_own_sagitta_about_the_axis` and `a_facet_over_the_axis_or_unreadable_is_never_round` (NaN and infinite input excuse nothing).
- `solid_law_goldens`' `contain_law` now names the holes it drills (it called the law with `hole_walls: true` and no holes, which now excuses nothing). Its verdicts are unchanged: all 14 goldens clean, and the drill/peck/tap 32-gon goldens still need, and keep, the excuse.
- Kept green without loosening anything: `bore_facet_sagitta` (2/2) and `bore_entry`.
- Full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head 6637e92c: green, 8.1 min. The sim lib plus 19 sim suites, motion `real_tip`/`solid_law`, the app lib plus 75 app suites: 950 passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored.
- By hand on the same head: `bore_facet_sagitta`, `golden_cl`, `conformance`, `tap_sim`, `mill2d_c`, `drill_prior_kinds`, `drilling_cross_box`, `drilling_cross_holder`: 57 passed, 0 failed. Before cleanup I also ran `bore_entry`, `verify`, `solid_law`, `solid_law_goldens`, `coarse_contain`, `drilling_*`, `operations` and more on identical logic, all green. (There is no `coarse_rims` suite on main.)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test hole_wall_flats --test solid_law_goldens -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens

No golden file moves: no `.cl`, `.nc` or snapshot PNG is touched, and `golden_cl` is green. I instrumented the old rule over the touched suites (throwaway, removed). Every excuse the old rule granted in `solid_law_goldens` (3326), `drilling_cross` (15595) and `operations` (574) is still granted.

The one newly convicted fixture is `tap_sim::a_tap_in_a_hole_modelled_at_tap_drill_size_is_not_a_gouge`:
- Its hole is a **square** of half-width 2.5 under an M6 tap.
- The generator's contain law sweeps the tap at its full r 3, which is 0.5 mm into each flat. The old rule excused that only because the square's corners (r 3.54) stand outside the tap.
- The test asserts only the program sim's verdict (core-radius tap, #266), so it still passes. The op's generator verdict now carries a blocking Gouge.
- This matches main on a *round* tap-drill hole, where the contain law already convicts the tap's full radius (the hole's vertices are inside the tap, so no excuse applied). The square was the bug's case, not a different law.

## Not exercised

- A tilted cross hole through a coarse wall: `drilling_cross*` suites pass, and the axis-in-frame mapping is covered only by them.
- A 4th/5th-axis posed Drill/Bore whose tool axis is not the hole axis: there the excuse now stands down (stricter).
- Real STEP/STL parts beyond `Milling-test.step`. A hole imported coarser than 0.05 mm sagitta (e.g. a 16-gon on r 5) now convicts as a false gouge, which is the safe side, as with #864.

## Overlap with PR #1099

This PR changes `solid.rs`, `solid_index.rs`, `mod.rs`, `contact.rs` and `rapids_posed.rs` (the `hits` signature: the `hole_walls: bool` parameter became the hole-axis slice `walls`). PR #1099 also changes them: it adds a `bores` parameter to the same `hits` and a `solid_hits_threaded` beside `solid_hits`, and `generate.rs` `contain_into`. Whichever merges second needs a careful keep-both on those lines. `swept.rs` `chord_dip` is gone: #1099's call to it becomes `hole_wall::wall_excuse`. #1099's own vertex-based measurements (`thread_bore.rs` `wall_radius`, `material_source.rs` `major_rims`) are left to that PR's review, which asks for this same nearest-point rule.

Changelog: The verifier no longer excuses a drill, bore, thread mill or cross drill cutting into the flats of a hole whose corners lie on its circle (an octagon, a D-bore, a square); only a round wall's own tessellation, up to 0.05 mm, is forgiven (#1205).

Effort: high (no escalation). Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 29); branched from upstream/main 62a2c93a.

Fixes #1205
